title: Why Adobe Agreed to a $150 Million Cancellation Fee Deal
alt_title_1: Inside the DOJ Case Over Adobe's 50% Early Termination Fee
alt_title_2: The Tiny Tooltip Behind Adobe's $150 Million DOJ Settlement
description_hook: On March 13, 2026, the U.S. Department of Justice announced that Adobe agreed to a $150 million settlement ($75 million in civil penalties plus $75 million in free services) to resolve federal allegations over hidden 50% early termination fees on Annual, Paid Monthly subscriptions.

affiliate_cta.offer_name: Free 48-Case Lawsuit & Refund Dossier + Forensics Reading List
affiliate_cta.pinned_comment: Did you ever get hit with Adobe's 50% early termination fee? Both DOJ filings are linked in the description.

scenes.headline: 50% Fee of Months Remaining
scenes.narration: That monthly Adobe price hid a 50 percent cancellation bill until the DOJ sued.
scenes.source: U.S. v. Adobe Inc., Complaint Para. 51-52, p. 11 (N.D. Cal.)

scenes.headline: Pre-Selected Annual Lock-In
scenes.narration: The DOJ complaint showed checkout defaulted to Annual, paid monthly while tucking terms behind a tooltip.
scenes.source: U.S. v. Adobe Inc., No. 5:24-cv-03630, Complaint p. 8 (N.D. Cal.)

scenes.headline: Adobe's $150M DOJ Deal
scenes.narration: In March 2026, Adobe agreed to a 150 million dollar settlement without admitting legal liability.
scenes.source: U.S. Department of Justice Press Release (Mar 13, 2026)

scenes.headline: $75M Penalty + $75M Credits
scenes.narration: That deal includes a 75 million dollar civil penalty, 75 million in user credits, and clearer exit flows.

scenes.headline: Paid Monthly Isn't Cancel Anytime
scenes.narration: Paid monthly rarely means cancel anytime. Open every billing tooltip before saving a card online.
scenes.source: Restore Online Shoppers' Confidence Act & DOJ Settlement (2026)

sources.label: DOJ Press Release: Adobe Agrees to $150M Settlement Under ROSCA (Mar 13, 2026)
DOJ Complaint: United States v. Adobe Inc., No. 5:24-cv-03630-BLF (N.D. Cal.)
